data.title: The Strong Earnings Posted By Zaptec (OB:ZAP) Are A Good Indication Of The Strength Of The Business
data.description:
Zaptec ASA's (OB:ZAP) earnings announcement last week was disappointing for investors, despite the decent profit numbers. Our analysis says that investors should be optimistic, as the strong profit is built on solid foundations.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

Zooming In On Zaptec's Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

For the year to September 2026, Zaptec had an accrual ratio of -0.72. That implies it has very good cash conversion, and that its earnings in the last year actually significantly understate its free cash flow. To wit, it produced free cash flow of kr394m during the period, dwarfing its reported profit of kr141.9m. Zaptec shareholders are no doubt pleased that free cash flow improved over the last twelve months.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Our Take On Zaptec's Profit Performance

As we discussed above, Zaptec's accrual ratio indicates strong conversion of profit to free cash flow, which is a positive for the company. Because of this, we think Zaptec's underlying earnings potential is as good as, or possibly even better, than the statutory profit makes it seem! Furthermore, it has done a great job growing EPS over the last year. The goal of this article has been to assess how well we can rely on the statutory earnings to reflect the company's potential, but there is plenty more to consider. In light of this, if you'd like to do more analysis on the company, it's vital to be informed of the risks involved. Case in point: We've spotted 1 warning sign for Zaptec you should be aware of.

This note has only looked at a single factor that sheds light on the nature of Zaptec's profit. But there are plenty of other ways to inform your opinion of a company. The Two Siemens Stories Investors Had In Front Of Them

The shares cost €227 at the start of the period, and Siemens investors were weighing two very different but plausible stories.

On the bullish side, one Narrative saw Fair Value at €246, 9% above the start price, built on 6.1% annual revenue growth and profit margins reaching 11.2% within about three years.

The more cautious view put Fair Value at €208, 8% below the start price, assuming 5.0% yearly revenue growth, a 17.0% profit margin over five years, and a future P/E of 18.0x.

Siemens later reported Q4 2026 revenue of €23,683m and net income of €2,191m, with net margin at 9.3% versus 7.7% a year earlier. That mix of higher sales, higher profit and a wider margin leaned toward the bullish case that expected healthier profitability, although it did not directly test the specific 11.2% or 17.0% margin targets yet.

The useful takeaway is simple. When a thesis hinges on better margins, track net margin alongside revenue and earnings in each report and check whether it is actually creeping toward the level the story needs.

data.title: What Greencore Group Doubters Overlooked
data.description:

Investors who held Greencore Group over the past year are up 35.1%, including dividends. If you were weighing a purchase back on 13 November 2025, what exactly did you need to believe about these moves before any of that later news arrived?

The Two Stories Investors Had To Choose Between On Greencore Group

The shares cost £2.29 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Greencore Group then had to decide which story felt closer to reality.

On the optimistic side, one narrative pointed to a Fair Value of £2.56, a rough guide to what the price might be if the thesis played out. That view leaned on the Making Business Easier program and a wider technology overhaul, which were expected to cut costs and lift future efficiency.

The more cautious narrative anchored on a Fair Value of £1.85 and focused on different pressures. Rising regulatory scrutiny of packaging and heavier reliance on a small group of UK retailers were treated as key risks to earnings stability.

What The Results Changed For The Greencore Group Thesis

Greencore Group raised profit guidance as volumes ran ahead of the sector and highlighted progress integrating Bakkavor, which supported the optimistic efficiency story. The same period brought harder figures to weigh. Revenue moved from £922m in H1 2025 to £1,318m in H1 2026, while net income swung from a £19.8m profit to a £34.8m loss and net margin fell to 2.6% below zero. The evidence cut both ways.

Solstad Maritime reported a tax benefit of US$30m, which is well worth noting. In the likely event the tax benefit is not repeated, we'd expect to see its statutory profit levels drop, at least in the absence of strong growth.
